methodology: Different fiber blends were prepared and tested to investigate the improvement in mechanical and air permeability properties of waste fiber material by adding wood kraft fibers (KF), hemp soda fibers (HF), and ammonium persulfate oxidated cellulose nanofibrils (CNF).
research_objective: Investigate whether the mechanical and air permeability properties of waste fiber material can be significantly improved by adding wood kraft fibers, hemp soda fibers, and ammonium persulfate oxidized cellulose nanofibrils.

key_findings.finding: Hemp fibers outperform wood fibers in improving recycled paper properties.
The addition of CNF depends on fiber composition and properties, requiring a modeling formula for different compositions.
The hornification process leads to semipermanent closure of the fibers' cell wall, resulting in decreased fiber quality during recycling.

Various approaches have been explored to address subpar performance of recycled fibers, including refining, incorporating dry strength additives, utilizing enzymes, and incorporating nanocellulose into the recycled pulp.
The mechanical properties of materials made of recycled fibers can be significantly improved by adding virgin wood and hemp fibers in different amounts.
The cooking process parameters include concentration of active alkali (NaOH), temperature, time, and liquor-to-wood ratio.

properties.value: semipermanent closure of fibers' cell wall
properties.context: described as a result of hornification process
Results revealed the excellence of hemp fibers over wood fibers regarding the improvement of WF products.

properties.value: dependent on fiber composition and properties
properties.context: The impact of CNF depended on fiber composition and properties. A formula for modeling the CNF impact on different fiber compositions was proposed.
Obtained fiber material samples showed suitability for home composting, thus contributing to the goals of the European Green Deal regarding reducing landfill waste and developing cleaner products.
